notes:
EVENT FACTS. Intel ISEF 2017 (68th ISEF) was held May 14-19, 2017 at the Los Angeles Convention Center, Los Angeles, California. Special awards were announced Thursday May 18 and Grand Awards Friday May 19, 2017. Finalists: sources vary between 'more than 1,775' (njrsf.org), 'about 1,778', 'nearly 1,800' (Society for Science blog) and 'nearly 2,000' (one Intel page); all agree on 78 countries, regions and territories and ~425 affiliated fairs. Roughly US$4 million in awards; about 600 finalists received grand awards. There were 22 categories in 2017 (the Society press release lists 22 Best of Category winners; one snexplores/Science News summary says '20'; American Bazaar says '22 Best of Category winners' - we found and verified all 22). Best of Category = US$5,000 plus a US$1,000 Intel Foundation grant to the winner's school and US$1,000 to the affiliated fair; First Award $3,000; Second $1,500; Third $1,000; Fourth $500. Each Best of Category winner also received a First Award in the same category (so the 22 BoC records are repeated in first_awards).

AWARDS THAT DID NOT EXIST IN 2017: Craig R. Barrett Award (2019+), H. Robert Horvitz Prize (2021+), Peggy Scripps Award (2022+), George D. Yancopoulos Innovator Award (2023+), Mary Sue Coleman Award. The top tier in 2017 = Gordon E. Moore Award ($75,000) + two Intel Foundation Young Scientist Awards ($50,000 each). The Dudley R. Herschbach SIYSS Award went to three finalists (Movsesian, Naidu, Pate; confirmed by the Society blog 'Teen cancer researchers meet Nobel Laureates in Stockholm' and 'Teen researching Parkinson's disease meets Nobel Prize winners'). The EUCYS award went to Kendra Zhang and Nicky Wojtania (Society blog 'Intel ISEF 2017 finalists take on Estonia'; EUCYS 2017 took place 22-27 Sept 2017 in Tallinn, Estonia).

CONFLICTS / DISCREPANCIES FOUND IN SEARCH SNIPPETS (kept both as instructed): (1) Biomedical and Health Sciences BoC: one snippet attributed the BoC to Sachin Jaishankar & Somil Jain (Hamilton HS, AZ, 'Developing a Nanoscale DLD Array Using Immunosignature-Derived Aptamers to Effectively Separate and Analyze Tumor Exosomes'); but that project is BCHM031T (a Biochemistry team project) and three independent results (science-fair.org, csef.usc.edu, SSP press release) give Daniel Zhang (Westview HS, CA) for BMED BoC - we keep Daniel Zhang; the Jaishankar/Jain grand-award level is unknown. (2) Biochemistry BoC: one snippet attached the RAD51 title to Jaishankar/Jain; the ACS Community page and the Society blog confirm Karina Movsesian - we keep Movsesian. (3) Energy: Chemical BoC: one snippet claimed Katherine Beadle (Bishop Feehan HS, MA, 'Analyzing Algal Lipid Content to Optimize Biofuel Production', EGCH010); other results say Beadle won a Fourth Award ($500) and that Kendra Zhang (Jericho HS, NY) won BoC + first place in Energy: Chemical (worldsciencefestival.com, Jericho district, Society Estonia blog) - we keep Kendra Zhang. (4) Behavioral and Social Sciences BoC: one snippet claimed Latifah Maratun Sholikhah (SMA Negeri 1 Teras, Boyolali, Indonesia, 'Neglected Children: Case Study of Public Attitudes toward Children with HIV AIDS in Six Sub-Districts in Surakarta'); Indonesian sources (ANTARA) say she won a FOURTH award in BEHA plus an APA honorable mention; Erin Smith is confirmed as BoC (abstract ProjectId=10383, Wikipedia) - we keep Smith. (5) Spelling: the Microbiology BoC winner appears as 'Rahul Subramaniam' (Greenwich Public Schools, Greenwich Time, LinkedIn) and 'Rahul Subramanian' (American Bazaar); Greenwich sources are authoritative - Subramaniam. (6) Two snippets attributed other winners' titles to Korean (Daegu-il Science HS, Seoul International School/Jaewoo Heo, MATS019 'Emergent Properties from WS2 Empowered by Laser Sculpting and Au Nanoparticles Landscaping') and Mexican (Jose Ocegueda Sanchez, CETI Jalisco) students as 'Best of Category' - these are summarizer errors (titles belong to Yegnesh and Miles); the award level of Heo and Ocegueda Sanchez is unknown. (7) ISTA (Ireland) gives the dates as 'May 11-16' and the VNU (Vietnam) page says the ceremony was 'May 20' - both wrong/time-zone; official dates are May 14-19 with the Grand Awards on May 19. (8) The Thai project 'Factors Affecting Polystyrene Foam Consuming Rate of Superworms (Zophobas morio)' (Nutchawara Moonkaew et al., Bunyawat Witthayalai School) was claimed by one snippet to be a BoC winner - false (Animal Sciences BoC = Dahl); its real award level is unknown. (9) Ayah Shehadeh & Bayan Abu Alragheb (Al-Hasaad Al-Tarbawi School, Jordan, 'Leading the Environment with Less Lead, Nano-Structured Jordanian Kaolinite for the Removal of Lead from Industrial Waste Water'): one snippet says First Award $3,000, the ACS page says Third Award $1,000 in Chemistry (the $3,000 may be a special award) - not placed in first_awards. (10) Chentian Li (Zhuhai, China, EBED033) is listed as a First Award from a single snippet of the Society press release - treat as 'probable'. (11) Shantanu Jakhete: one snippet says both 'Second Award' and 'First Award' in Animal Sciences; SSEF Florida supports Second Award ($1,500).

OTHER COUNTRY/REGION RESULTS (lower-tier, from affiliated-fair/press pages): Germany - 13-member Jugend forscht team won 16 prizes; Tassilo Schwarz also won AIAA $2,000, Patent and Trademark Office Society $500, CASTIC trip, INCOSE and NSA honorable mentions. Ireland (ISTA/SciFest) - Conor Foy (Colaiste Chiarain, Croom, Limerick) won the Society for Experimental Mechanics $2,500 special award plus a category award; Paul Clarke (St. Paul's College, Raheny, Dublin) won AMS $250. Taiwan (MOE) - three Third Awards (Yeh Chia-yu, Chung Shan Industrial & Commercial School, Embedded Systems 'Eco paper circuit printer & its applications'; Chen Yi-chen & Wu Yun-ching, Taipei First Girls HS, Chemistry 'High efficiency TADF-based transparent OLEDs'; Lin Juei-yin, Taipei First Girls HS, Mathematics 'Which maps are 4-list colorable?') and one Fourth Award (Angel Huang, Taipei American School, folate status). Vietnam - Pham Quang Huy (Quang Tri Town HS) Third Award in Robotics; Tran Dan Khue & Vu Nam Anh (VNU HS for Gifted Students) Fourth Award Chemistry; Chu Hoang Minh Duc & Pham Thien Tan (Le Hong Phong HS) Fourth Award. Turkiye (TUBITAK) - 4 of 10 projects awarded; best was Fourth Award for Dilge Kocabas & Dilara Alev Ortel (Izmir Ozel Takev) 'Aptaliposomes' bio-detectors; Hamdi Goktan Ozmenekse & Ata Aydin Uslu (Edirne Suleyman Demirel Fen Lisesi) AMS special award in Mathematics. Indonesia - 4 of 14 students awarded (incl. Sholikhah, Fourth Award BEHA). Philippines - Davao City NHS team Second Award in Plant Sciences; Carl Joshua Quines (Valenzuela City School of Mathematics and Science) awarded in Mathematics for 'Bounds on the Metric Dimensions for Families of Planar Graphs'. Saudi Arabia (SPA/Mawhiba) - reported 18 grand awards and 18 special awards (names not individually verified). India - Prashaant Ranganathan BoC; paddy-seedling team Second Award Plant Sciences. China - Chentian Li (EBED033) First Award (probable); Shilun Li (Guangdong Experimental HS) and He Huang (YK Pao School) honorable mentions. Brazil - Isabela Dombrady, Julia Rolim, Maria Gabriela Leal (Colegio Giordano Bruno) special award for 'Self-Image of Athletes with Disability: A New Meaning'. France - Jean-Baptiste Flieller & Elias Suvanto (Gymnase Jean Sturm, Strasbourg) AGI first place special award for 'Study and Modeling of Pressure and Temperature during a Geyser Eruption' (relevant geoscience/volcanic topic). USA extras: Neha Hulkund (Tesla STEM HS, WA) Third Award CBIO 'The Application of Machine Learning Algorithms on EEG Data to Predict and Detect Epileptic Seizures'; Matthew Hase-Liu (Lynbrook HS, CA) Third Award Mathematics; Kavya Kopparapu, Neeyanth Kopparapu & Justin Zhang (TJHSST) Third Award TMED 'Inexpensive Mobile Diagnosis of Diabetic Retinopathy Using Deep Learning'; Rucha Joshi (Westwood HS, Austin TX) NSA Science of Security first place $3,000 (special award); Michael Litt (Orange HS, OH) NSA Science of Security $3,000 (special award) 'MATCHLESS: A Linear Algebraic Approach to Duplicate File Identification'; Catherine Chen (Academy for Health and Medical Sciences, NJ) Fourth Award. Kentucky items (Madison Sneve, Govind Krishna, duPont Manual) surfaced with inconsistent amounts and could not be verified before the session's web-search budget (200 calls) ran out.

CATEGORIES NOT FOUND: none - all 22 Best of Category winners for 2017 were identified and cross-checked against at least two independent sources where possible. Second/First award lists are partial (regional-page angle); the official full list lives on the Society for Science 2017 Grand Awards press release, which could not be fetched directly (societyforscience.org, njrsf.org, nwse.org all blocked by the egress proxy).
